examples.name: Default
examples.summary: A relative range (`Last 15 minutes`) that stays relative: the value is `{ type: 'relative', amount, unit }`, re-resolved against the clock on every query. The panel has two tabs, Relative and Absolute, and opens on Relative here because the value is relative (an absolute or `since` value opens Absolute). Relative lists the quick ranges and a **Custom range** row that opens a duration and unit form in their place (Back to quick ranges returns); Absolute shows the month grid first, with Month and Year selects between the arrows to jump far back, then the start and end date and time, typed or picked from a 30-minute list. Refresh every is on at 5 minutes by default, so the page handles `@refresh` by re-running its query. The panel is as thin as the calendar and commits nothing until Apply; the page states the time zone next to the picker (see the Events explorer block). Unset, `min` is five years ago and `max` the end of today. On a phone it opens as a full-width sheet from the bottom of the screen.

examples.name: Absolute
examples.summary: `range-selector-mode="absolute-only"` with a `max`: only the grid and the date and time fields, the trigger prints the range in the zone with its UTC offset, and Apply refuses an end before the start or past the limit with an inline message.

examples.name: RelativeOnly
examples.summary: `range-selector-mode="relative-only"` with the default quick ranges (Today to Last year) above the Custom range row, for a metrics interval that is always measured back from now.
